sentences.text: The petitioner pleads that he is running a grocery shop under the name and style of Kaviya Stores at Main Bazaar, Thattarmadam Village, Sathankulam Town, Thoothukudi District.
He states this shop is his only source of income.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis
He pleads that on 21.11.2024 he was away at Azhapula, Kerala, to attend a family wedding.

During that time, the third respondent/ Inspector of Police, Thattarmadam Police Station, registered a complaint against him in Crime No.145 of 2024 invoking Section 24(1) of Cigarette and other Tobacco Products Act, 2003 (hereinafter referred to as 'COPTA').

entities.text: Cigarette and other Tobacco Products Act, 2003
entities.label: STATUTE

sentences.text: The petitioner further pleads that he runs a grocery shop and has nothing to do with tobacco products.
He alleges that the third respondent/ Inspector of Police registered the case to meet the statistical targets set by his superiors.
4. Based on the FIR, the second respondent proceeded and sealed the premises under the impugned order.
Hence, this writ petition.
5. I heard Mr.M.Muthumanikkam, learned Government Advocate, who takes notice for the respondents 1 and 2 and Mr.M.Karunanithi, learned Government Advocate, who takes notice for the third respondent.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 08/04/2025 06:38:33 pm )
6. The basis for sealing the premises is the registration of FIR under Section 24(1) of COPTA.
The third respondent had prepared a final report and filed the same before the learned Judicial Magistrate at Sathankulam in Crl.M.P.No.5010 of 2024.

The learned Judicial Magistrate, however,
had refused to take the final report on file and rejected it, coming to a clear and categorical conclusion that there is no violation or contravention of Section 6 of the COPTA.
The learned Judicial Magistrate has further held that no offence had been made out under Section 24 of COPTA.

Given this, for the second respondent to refer the FIR and direct sealing of the premises three Highcourt Raja vs The Commissioner on 24 March, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/158193654/
2 months thereafter, reflects patent non-application of mind, as well as a significant divergence in the sharing of information between the respondents 1 and 2 and the third respondent.
7. A perusal of the impugned order shows that the second respondent has relied upon the FIR in Crime No.145 of 2024.

As pointed out above, since the FIR resulted in a final report, which was subsequently rejected by the learned Judicial Magistrate, it does not lie within the powers of the second respondent to insist that the crime still exists.
https://www.mhc.tn.gov.in/judis ( Uploaded on: 08/04/2025 06:38:33 pm )
8. In the light of the above discussion, I have no other option than to interfere the impugned order.
Accordingly, the impugned order of Na.Ka.No.En.4538/A2/2024/U.Paa.A-327/N-2, dated 05.03.2025, passed by the second respondent is hereby quashed.
The offence itself has not been made out, it is open to the petitioner to de-seal the premises and re- enter them.
9. With the above direction, this Writ Petition is allowed.
No costs.
